name: Partners of each bracket
brief:
A pricing formula uses `()`, `[]` and `{}` and is known to be well formed. An editor wants to highlight each bracket's partner.

Write `bracket_partners(formula)`, which returns a list of `(open, close)` tuples of indices, one per bracket pair, sorted by the opening index. Other characters are ignored.

Example. For `'f(a[0], {b})'` the answer is `[(1, 11), (3, 5), (8, 10)]`: the round bracket at 1 closes at 11, the square one at 3 closes at 5, and the curly one at 8 closes at 10.
constraints: $O(n)$ or $O(n \log n)$ time is the target. Scanning back from every closer is too slow on deep nesting.
All the tests in a run share one 5-second limit in the browser.
hint: Push the index of each opener. A closer belongs to the opener on top of the stack, so pop it and record the pair. Pairs come out in closing order, so put them in opening order at the end.

examples.note: The outer round pair wraps the other two, so it opens first and closes last.
Two pairs side by side, each closing straight after it opens.

how: Submit runs 12 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: The most recent open bracket is the one a closer matches, and a stack of indices gives it at once.
Pairs are found in closing order, so sort them by opening index before returning.
Each bracket is pushed or popped once; the final sort costs $O(n \log n)$, or fill a list by opening index for $O(n)$.
